free_tier.stated: Jetstream2 prices every instance in ACCESS service units at 1 SU per vCPU per hour on CPU flavours and 2 SU per vCPU per hour on GPU and Large Memory flavours. A full A100 card flavour (g3.xl, 32 vCPU, 120 GB RAM, 40 GB GPU RAM) costs 64 SU per hour; a half-card (g3.large, 16 vCPU, 20 GB GPU RAM) costs 32 SU per hour; a quarter-card (g3.medium, 8 vCPU, 10 GB GPU RAM) costs 16 SU per hour. The smallest ACCESS tier, Explore, carries 400,000 credits, so 400,000 / 64 = 6,250 hours of a full A100 card, 12,500 hours of a half card, or 400,000 vCPU-hours on CPU flavours.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: This is the conversion the ACCESS record lacked: an Explore allocation is not 400,000 abstract credits but 6,250 A100-hours or 400,000 vCPU-hours, which turns the ACCESS tier from a benchmark allowance into roughly a year of a single always-on A100 at 16 hours a day. It composes badly with the free GPU vendors, because the same workload that fits a 40 GB card on Jetstream2 fits a 16 GB T4 elsewhere only after splitting.

notes: This finding changes compute/access: that record states the 400,000 credit limit but does not convert it, so a reader cannot tell whether Explore buys an afternoon or a year. The division is shown above and uses only rates from the two vendor pages. The cheapest paid shape is not applicable: Jetstream2 sells nothing for cash, and the credits are not purchasable, so the alternative to the institutional gate is not money. Note that stopped instances are still charged 75 percent and shelved instances are charged nothing, which changes the effective hours for an interactive workload. No account was created, so the rung is documented rather than measured.
